glosses: To quickly lower (the head or body), often in order to prevent it from being struck by something.

examples.text:

To arms by thirst of honour led,
When at a skirmish first he hears
The bullets whistling round his ears,
Will duck his head aside
Rimmer ducked his body low into his chair, so just his head remained above the table top, and peered past the backs of the examinees in front of him, waiting for the adjudicator to make his move.

glosses: To lower (something) into water; to thrust or plunge under liquid and suddenly withdraw.

examples.text: Adams after ducking the Squire tvvice or thrice leaped out of the Tub, […]

glosses: To evade doing something, especially something considered a responsibility.

examples.text: Victorian women choosing to duck the demands of domestic life to spend their time doing something they enjoyed is hardly a novel idea.

glosses: To lower the volume of (a sound) so that other sounds in the mix can be heard more clearly.

examples.text: The music is ducked under the voice.

examples.text: I'm just going to duck into the loo for a minute; can you hold my bag?

examples.text: Aussi je ne prétends pas un instant esquiver, de la part de ceux qui liront ces lignes, le reproche d’immoralité.

glosses: Se retirer sans rien dire et en évitant d’être aperçu, d’une compagnie, d’un lieu où l’on ne veut pas demeurer.

examples.text: Aussi, un beau matin, se sentant mieux, il avait laissé ses éperons d'or en paiement au pharmacopole, et s'était esquivé.
